verdict: REVISE — the sizing truth is exact on every surface it touches (schedule cells print the deepened size verbatim with zero label leak; takeoff SKUs shift by exactly the member delta; low-snow paper is byte-equal to master file-for-file; MN deepens ONLY past 71"; foundation/electrical/roof/MEP sheets byte-equal even in deepened states — the shared transform held, no B6-class drift), but the batch's own honesty device never reaches paper: the assumption 'sized per Table R602.7(1) @ 70 psf ground snow — ≤ 24 ft building width, roof-and-ceiling loading assumed' rides all 17 VT header member LABELS (dump grep: 17/17) and prints NOWHERE on the 18-sheet set, the takeoff CSV, or the cut list (grep 'R602.7|snow|24 ft' across every sheet: zero). That is the B6-shed class (statement only in code), and here it is load-bearing: the demo footprint measures ~10 m ≈ 33 ft on the printed plan — PAST the assumed 24 ft — and the batch's own encoded 70-psf/36-ft cell caps 2-2x10 at 4'-5" (53"), i.e. at true width the code's table would demand 4x12 where the VT schedule prints an unconditional 4x10 beside a 4'-8.63" RO (W1/W10/W11, png-pin/straddle-VT/12). A VT plans examiner cannot see from the submitted set that the header sizes hinge on an unverified width bound — while the SAME sheet 17/18 prints B9's equivalent assumption ('CS-WSP continuous sheathing assumed — R602.10 panel length/spacing not verified') as flags, so the set is internally inconsistent about which structural assumptions it confesses. One narrow, byte-safe fix closes the round: when spec.headerAssumption is set, surface it ONCE on paper — a compute-level warning (B9 grammar → P4 flag block prints it verbatim) and/or a general-note line beside the framing sheet's STUDS callout; low-snow output stays byte-equal by construction since the assumption is unset there. Geometry, marks, takeoff and jurisdiction byte-story all PASS and need no further rounds.
